name: Te Kāhui Manu Hōkai Māori GIS Association
story: Te Kāhui Manu Hōkai is the Māori GIS Association, a professional and community network supporting Māori participation in geographic information work. LINZ identifies it among New Zealand’s geospatial communities and records its collaboration on practical mapping wānanga.

From October 2020, Te Kāhui Manu Hōkai worked with LINZ on Ngā Poutama Matawhenua sessions, with support from GIS Journey Limited. The programme links practical GIS learning to iwi, Māori trusts and environmental groups.
The association’s collaboration brought Māori-led expertise into a programme supported by LINZ and GIS Journey, with regular wānanga shaped around the mapping needs of participating groups.

contentSections.title: Documented contribution in 2019
paragraphs: The association’s PLACE19 programme records more than 100 delegates in Rotorua in November 2019. Its five streams covered people, landscapes, assets, communication and education, with programme support from LINZ and sponsorship from Massey University and other spatial organisations.
